I farm 30 mu in Quzhou. Same land every year — wheat in winter, then maize after the wheat comes off in June. I also keep about 5 mu for stevia because the buyer pays good money if the leaves come out clean. So 25 mu goes to wheat-maize rotation, 5 mu to stevia.

For wheat, I plant Jimai variety like most people in my village — the seed dealer brings it every autumn and my neighbor Old Wang gets 520-550 kg/mu with it, so I stick with what works. I plough the land deep after the maize stalks come off, then put down two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15, about 50 kg per mu) before sowing. When spring comes and the wheat stands up at jointing, I top-dress with one bag of urea per mu, about 20 kg. That gives around 30 kg nitrogen total. I water the winter water before freezing, then jointing water, heading water, and grain-filling water — four times from my well. I spray twice, once for aphids and once against wheat scab if the weather turns wet at flowering. Last year I got 500 kg/mu, this year I aim for the same.

For maize after wheat, I use hybrid Zhengdan or Xianyu — everyone plants hybrid now, no one uses old seed anymore. No ploughing, just rotary till through the wheat stubble and seed with the planter. I side-dress about 40 kg of compound fertilizer at sowing, then 15 kg urea when the maize is knee-high. Maize is thirsty but the rainy season helps — I only irrigate once or twice if July is dry. One spray for corn borer. I expect 550-600 kg/mu.

Stevia is different — it needs richer ground and more care. I transplant seedlings in April, water more often (6 times through summer because we harvest the leaves 2-3 times), and put more compound fertilizer plus extra potash because the buyer wants good leaf quality. I spray 3 times to keep leaves clean. Yield is lower in kg but the price is much better.

I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield — a bad harvest ruins the year, some extra urea is just money.
